title: CommandResponse
description: The application/json body ClashEngine returns for every command POST (command.schema.json). HTTP status stays 200 whenever a well-formed command was processed -- `status` carries the semantic outcome; non-200 is reserved for transport-level faults (401 bad api key, 400 undecodable body, 404 unknown path, 503 engine busy). Consumers should key their handling on `status` + `result`, treating `detail` as human-readable explanation only.

schemaVersion.description: Wire format version, shared with command.schema.json.

commandId.description: The request's commandId, echoed verbatim (null when the request carried none or was undecodable).

status.description: ok: the desired state now holds (including idempotent no-ops like dequeueing a player who wasn't queued). rejected: the engine refused the change -- `result` says why. error: the command itself was malformed (unknown type, missing field, bad version); nothing was attempted.

result.description: Machine-readable outcome. For status=ok, one of the first block (already_queued_refreshed = the repeat enqueue refreshed the AFK dwell clock). For status=rejected, the engine's reason; not_connected / in_match / in_timeout / duplicate_player name the offending player in `player`. For status=error, what was wrong with the command.

detail.description: Human-readable elaboration (e.g. which field was missing, the offending player's remaining timeout). Never required for correct handling.

player.description: On per-player rejections (not_connected / in_match / in_timeout / duplicate_player), the in-game name of the player that caused it -- for group and form_match commands this may be someone other than the caller.

matchId.description: On form_match ok: the new match's id, correlating to match.started / match.ended events and cancel_match.

removedQueues.description: On dequeue ok: the registry ids of the queues the player was actually removed from (empty when they weren't queued anywhere the command covered).
